text: This is one function: a small card fight. It asks for dice, a player, a screen and a count. It never says who answers.
Each question is an effect. It travels out to a handler, and the handler also gets the rest of the function, called k.
Stack handlers around it. A scripted player and a screen give the same fight on every run.
Swap in a random bot and take the screen away. The function does not change.
Add a recorder, and thirty-two answers replay the whole fight, with no dice and no player.
A Monte Carlo bot answers a question by running the fight itself, while the fight that asked waits as k.
Run a hundred fights at once, each with its own dice. The random bot wins seventy-three. The Monte Carlo bot wins all one hundred.
One function, unchanged, in every stack. That is algebraic effects in Python, with doeff.
